headline: PNP Reports 26 Storm and Monsoon Deaths as Cyclone Stays Offshore
seoTitle: PNP Reports 26 Storm and Monsoon Deaths as Cyclone Stays Offshore
seoDescription: The PNP reported 26 deaths linked to recent storms and monsoon rains, subject to NDRRMC validation, while PAGASA tracked a tropical depression far east of Northern Luzon and outside the PAR.
deck: Police reported 26 deaths linked to recent storms and monsoon rains, with the tally still subject to validation, while PAGASA tracked a tropical depression far east of Northern Luzon and outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine National Police reported at least 26 deaths linked to recent storms and southwest monsoon rains. PNP spokesperson Allen Rae Co said the police figures remained subject to validation by the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council and other agencies.

The police breakdown cited 16 deaths from landslides in the Cordillera Administrative Region, seven in Rizal, two in La Union and Pangasinan, and one police officer in Cadiz City. The count is therefore a preliminary PNP report rather than a final national disaster tally.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: In its 4 a.m. August 12 weather report, PAGASA said the southwest monsoon was affecting Luzon. The agency forecast cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over several western Luzon areas, with possible flash floods or landslides from moderate to at times heavy rain.

PAGASA also tracked a tropical depression outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility, about 1,990 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon at 3 a.m. The system had maximum sustained winds of 55 kilometers per hour and gusts up to 70 kilometers per hour and was moving east-northeastward at 30 kilometers per hour. The available PAGASA report did not say the distant cyclone was strengthening the monsoon.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Preliminary casualty figures can change as local and national agencies reconcile reports, but the toll underscores the continuing risks from saturated slopes, flooding and dangerous travel conditions. Clear attribution prevents an early police count from being mistaken for a finalized government total.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a validated NDRRMC casualty report, updated local warnings and PAGASA's next advisory on both the southwest monsoon and the offshore tropical depression. Residents in flood- and landslide-prone areas should follow current local evacuation and weather instructions.
